Open the map page

1
US 'defensive' strikes on Qeshm (2 Nov)
A US official said limited strikes hit Iranian targets on Qeshm Island after Iranian surface-to-air missile fire at US assets; IRNA reported five explosions (exact sites not given).
2
Ships hit off Musandam and Oman (29 Oct–2 Nov)
Tug SELAT STORM partly sank NW of Musandam and a vessel was holed off Lima, Oman on 1 Nov, after limpet-mine hits 25 nm NE of Khasab on 30 Oct; an Indian cargo vessel was hit near Oman on 2 Nov, one killed (zone approximate).
3
Hormuz ~14 mb/d (wk to 18 Oct)
Kpler: about 14 mb/d in the week to 18 Oct, 82% of pre-war 17.1 mb/d; no newer weekly figure published.
4
Tanker hit 72 nm E of Ras Al Khafji (1 Nov)
UKMTO: a south-east-bound tanker was hit on its port side by two projectiles at 23:47 UTC on 1 Nov, about 72 nm east of Ras Al Khafji; crew safe.
5
113 ships holding in Gulf (2 Nov), from 128
straits.live counted 113 AIS-visible ships holding in the Strait and Gulf watch box on 2 Nov, down from 128 on 1 Nov; JMIC counted about 492 waiting outside the strait on 25 Oct (area approximate).
6
LNG carrier AL MAYEDA hit (30 Oct)
The Qatari LNG carrier was hit by three projectiles around 18:00 UTC on 30 Oct, about 40 nm south of Lavan Island; no injuries, ship operational.
7
Bypass routes >40% of Gulf exports
Kpler: pipelines avoiding Hormuz carry over 40% of regional exports vs 17% pre-war; Yanbu loadings 2.21 mb/d in 1-25 Oct vs 2.54 in September.
GULF OIL FLOWS · updated 3 Nov 2026

Oil still moves through Hormuz below pre-war: Kpler's latest weekly figure is about 14 mb/d in the week to 18 Oct (82% of the 17.1 mb/d pre-war), and Kpler puts Saudi loadings for 1-25 Oct at 2.95 mb/d from Ras Tanura and 2.21 mb/d from Yanbu, both below September. Ships kept being hit around Musandam and Oman: a tug partly sank north-west of Musandam and a vessel was holed off Lima, Oman on 1 Nov, and an Indian cargo vessel was struck near Oman on 2 Nov, killing a sailor. On the eve of the 3 Nov midterms the US carried out limited 'defensive' strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island after Iranian missile fire at US assets, while Trump said Iran 'wants a settlement' and Iran says Hormuz could reopen within two days if its conditions are met. AIS-visible ships holding in the Gulf eased to 113 on 2 Nov from 128 the day before; bypass routes still carry over 40% of regional exports.
